system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

The Seller’s **[STANDARD] labels and “reviewer efficiency note” are not evidence of Buyer agreement**. All positions remain reviewable. The recommendations below are Buyer negotiating positions, subject to the full SPA and underlying DD documents, which have not been provided.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap; seek **50% / AUD 12m**, with separate treatment for protected categories below. | **Reject 20% as proposed:** it leaves Buyer bearing most warranty risk on a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Seek **AUD 10,000 de minimis**, **AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, aggregation of related claims and no application to protected categories. | **Counter:** the combined thresholds can exclude significant cumulative losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Seek **24 months** for general warranties; timely notified claims survive expiry, with reasonable notification requirements and separate category deadlines. | **Reject blanket extension:** Buyer needs adequate discovery time without unintentionally shortening other remedies. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title have the same cap and deadline as general warranties. | Separate capacity/title warranties, **100% price cap**, no de minimis/basket, and a longer contractual notification period—seek **seven years**, subject to applicable statutory limits. | **Reject:** ownership and authority are foundational acquisition risks, not ordinary operational warranties. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | No express carve-out supplied; limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Express preservation of claims for Seller fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment, including appropriate attribution of representatives’ conduct; no contractual caps, thresholds or deadlines for those claims. | **Insist on express carve-outs throughout:** Seller must not obtain contractual protection for its own fraud or exclude non-excludable liability. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only **fair disclosure**, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; specific warranty cross-references and a frozen, indexed disclosure record. Specific indemnities must survive disclosure. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure:** document availability is not adequate identification of the risk being transferred to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters merely discoverable from records. | Prefer no knowledge exclusion; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel at signing, without constructive/imputed knowledge or a duty to investigate. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-wide attribution:** diligence should not become a blanket waiver of Seller warranties. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence of conditions being satisfied. | Buyer-waivable condition precedent requiring effective consent **and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions**, without materially adverse amendments; verify the underlying contract. | **Require substantive satisfaction before Completion:** approximately 30% of FY26 revenue is exposed, and a conditional letter may not resolve the risk. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release supplied after Completion. | Verified payout figures, repayment at Completion and effective releases of all relevant security, guarantees and change-control defaults through agreed closing arrangements. Reflect debt in the funds flow without double counting. | **Reject unsecured post-Completion delivery:** debt-free/cash-free pricing requires debt discharge and an effective release mechanism at closing. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses described as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Establish obligor, eligibility and timing; Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs through payment or an agreed price adjustment, backed by an indemnity. | **Itemise and allocate expressly:** a Seller-side description does not prevent the acquired company from carrying the liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, but non-payment is not independently verified. | Verify payment and chain of title; obtain cleared-payment evidence and an effective confirmatory assignment before Completion. Cover losses from the identified ownership defect, including remediation and third-party claims, under a separate indemnity. | **Broaden protection beyond the fee:** paying the invoice alone may not establish ownership or compensate for consequences of defective title. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and unlikely material; access, exact scope and notification duties remain unresolved. | Prompt independent factual/legal assessment, evidence preservation, containment and legally required notifications; agreed updates and a specific indemnity for the identified pre-Completion incident, with proportionate security if warranted. | **Investigate and allocate the risk without prejudging breach:** neither unauthorised access nor absence of material exposure is established. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Review DD-008/DD-011 together for commitment dates, scope, termination rights, accruals and ordinary-course status; require consent for material new commitments and consistent purchase-price treatment. | **Reserve the classification pending evidence:** related renewals must be assessed together, but are not automatically debt-like or Seller liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to Claims of every nature. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and payment/price-adjustment obligations, with fraud overrides and tailored remedies, caps and deadlines. | **Reject the omnibus approach:** general warranty protections must not unintentionally defeat debt repayment, indemnities or other substantive obligations. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s share register identifying Seller as 100% holder. | Independently reconcile the register, corporate records, certificates and allotment/transfer history; check encumbrances, options, convertibles and third-party rights; obtain title warranties and proper transfer deliverables. | **Verify rather than accept the register alone:** it records ownership but does not establish an unencumbered, fully diluted 100% acquisition by itself. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP treated as settled under the general warranty regime. | Keep both open: a pre-Completion tax indemnity with appropriate exclusions and a statutory assessment-period-plus-buffer deadline; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties with separately negotiated limits and survival, plus Ironquay-specific protection. | **Reopen expressly:** latent tax exposure and core IP risks require tailored treatment, not assumed acceptance of the general regime. |

**Closing priorities:** resolve Bluefen consent conditions, Riverlark discharge mechanics, bonus funding, Ironquay title evidence and the incident investigation before accepting the Seller’s proposed allocation of risk.
=== END ADVICE ===
